story.html: Onosato was already an Ozeki when the tracker switched on, and the rest of the climb took him less than a year. He won championships in back-to-back tournaments in March and May 2025, then a third in September 2025, and that last one carried him to Yokozuna. His shikona means "great village," handed down the line from Takanosato and Kisenosato, the master who trained him. He fights in a midnight blue mawashi. Reaching the top rank that fast is rare, and his record across the climb is the plain explanation for it.

Won opening day but with heavy back-pedaling and a pull the booth called beneath a Yokozuna, and they warned the retreating frog-jump style could itself invite injury. Read as more mental than physical now. [booth: Raja]

bio.v: Style (booth): left-hand otsuke into a right-hand inside position is his bread and butter. Watch item (flaw): a tendency to back-pedal and pull (hatakikomi) when pressured at the tachiai, the booth's repeated criticism on opening day, and a risk to his own footing. [Grand Sumo Live, booth, as of 2026-09-13]

大の里 (O-no-sato) = 大 great + の (of) + 里 village → literally 'great village.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on characters, but this is a LINEAGE name: '-nosato' places him in the line of yokozuna Takanosato (隆の里) and his master Kisenosato (稀勢の里); 大 chosen to accentuate his talent.

story.html: Kirishima has done the hard thing in sumo, which is fall and climb back. He had been an Ozeki, lost the rank, and opened the crew era down in the maegashira, grinding through the named ranks again and again. The reward came at the March 2026 basho: a championship from Sekiwake, and with it a return to Ozeki. He carries the name of his stablemaster, the former Yokozuna Kirishima, and it means "mist island," which is also a volcanic range in Kyushu. He wrestled his earlier career as Kiribayama. The mawashi is a deep brownish purple.

bio.v: Style (booth): versatility and ring sense, an array of weapons and a sharp feel for where he is on the straw, which lets him stay calm under a forward-moving opponent. Watch item: a habit of backing up and pulling when off balance. [Grand Sumo Live, booth, as of 2026-09-13]
霧島 (Kirishima) = 霧 (mist) + 島 (island) → 'Mist Island' (also the Kirishima volcanic range in Kyushu). Confidence: HIGH. Lineage: inherited from his stablemaster, former yokozuna Kirishima.

records.note: For Aonishiki, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: When the tracker switched on in March 2025, Aonishiki was a Maegashira 15 at the bottom of the top division; about eighteen months later he had climbed all the way to Ozeki. The Ukrainian came up through Komusubi and Sekiwake and collected three championships on the way: Kyushu 2025 as a Sekiwake, January 2026 on the run that first made him Ozeki, and July 2026, where he added a Technique prize after a slip back to Sekiwake. That July run was the wild one. He fought the whole basho on a bad left toe, took out both reigning Yokozuna on back-to-back days, clinched his Ozeki return, and then won the cup in a three-way playoff, all on the same foot. His shikona reads as "blue brocade," a tip of the cap to his master Aminishiki of the Ajigawa stable, with the blue nodding to the flag he came up under. He has favored a British racing green mawashi and a dark muted blue-grey. To the crew, he's just AO.

story.html: Atamifuji is young and pointed upward. He climbed through the maegashira ranks to the named ranks, picking up a Fighting Spirit prize at the July 2026 basho along the way. The name is a hometown flag: "Atami" is the hot-spring town he comes from and "Fuji" is the mountain, so the shikona reads as Atami's Fuji. He wears a dark, muted raspberry red. The crew calls him Atomic.

bio.v: Style (booth): the 'bellybop,' an agaburi-yori. Migi-yotsu with immense tachiai pressure; his turn-key is the left-hand outside grip. Once he locks it he solidifies his stance and forces the opponent out, and he is patient, in no rush to finish even without the right-hand inside. [Grand Sumo Live, booth, as of 2026-09-13]
熱海富士 (Atamifuji) = 熱海 (Atami, his hometown — lit. 'hot sea') + 富士 (Mt. Fuji) → "Atami's Fuji." Confidence: HIGH. Context: names his hometown Atami; Fuji connotes strength/majesty.

story.html: Hakunofuji arrived as one of Isegahama's most-hyped prospects and has the name changes to prove it. He came up as Ochiai, then took the shikona Hakuoho, a tribute built to evoke Hakuho and the Taiho line. He later became Hakunofuji and climbed to his first named rank at Komusubi. He wears a medium grey-brown mawashi. He is young, and one to watch.

story.html: Kotoshoho already has the thing most men on this page are still chasing: a championship. He won it from Maegashira 15 at the July 2025 basho, the kind of rank-and-file title that upends a tournament, and climbed to Sekiwake on the strength of it. He is the elder Koto brother, Sadogatake through and through, and came up as Kototebakari. His shikona reads as "koto victory peak." He wears a light blue-grey mawashi.

story.html: Takayasu is one of the elder statesmen of the division, a former Ozeki who still trades with the best of them. At the July 2026 basho he took a Fighting Spirit prize, won in a long grind over Asanoyama in the Nagoya heat that, oddly, seemed to ease his chronic bad back. One booth note the crew logged: his mawashi is famously tight, wrapped so hard that opponents cannot get a finger or a nail under it, which is a big part of why nobody can find a grip on him. He fights in a dark blue mawashi. Around the crew he is Hairy, or Papayasu.

story.html: Gonoyama is a powerhouse who has ranged across the maegashira ranks. The "go" in his name is inherited from his master, the former Ozeki Goeido, now the Takekuma stablemaster, and the shikona reads as "mountain of strength." He came up as Nishikawa. He fights in a midnight blue mawashi.

story.html: Takanosho is a former Sekiwake and a solid upper-maegashira presence, with the pushing-and-thrusting build to trouble anyone on a given day. His shikona reads as "prosperous victory." He came up under the name Masunosho before settling on this one. He fights in a red mawashi.

story.html: Roga has worked through the middle and lower maegashira across the crew era, with a dip into juryo early on. He was born in Kyzyl, in the Russian republic of Tuva, and took Mongolian nationality at 15, which is why the JSA first listed him as Mongolian though he has always said he is Russian. He fights out of the Futagoyama stable, and his shikona is one of the better ones on the banzuke: "elegant wolf." He came up as Roga Chikara. He wears a dark blue-purple mawashi.

bio.v: 狼雅 (Roga) = 狼 (ro, wolf) + 雅 (ga, elegant/refined) → 'Elegant wolf.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Russian-born, Futagoyama stable.

story.html: Asanoyama is a former Ozeki on the way back. The tracker caught him down in juryo in late 2025, and from there he has climbed back up through the division. His shikona reads as "morning mountain," the "asa" marking him as a Takasago man, and he fought earlier as Ishibashi. He wears a deep plum purple mawashi. A former top-ranker rebuilding in real time is one of the more compelling arcs on the board.

story.html: Fujiseiun spent much of 2025 in juryo before breaking through to the maegashira ranks. His shikona pairs the Fujishima "fuji" with "seiun," an idiom for lofty ambition, so it reads as something like "wisteria of high aspirations." He fights in a midnight blue mawashi. The climb out of juryo and the name both point the same direction.

story.html: Takerufuji comes with one of the great debut stories in the sport: he won a top-division championship in his very first makuuchi tournament, a genuine sensation. An Isegahama man, his shikona reads as "noble Fuji," and he came up as Ishioka. He is from Aomori and fights in a medium lilac purple mawashi.

layers.text: 26AkD3 (Scorekeeper Eye): Lots of cupping bruises over the back. (Jennie)

RULE SET THAT DAY (Jennie): cupping marks LOG, on the reasoning that cupping is no different in kind from tape - something hurts, and the treatment is the visible evidence of it. The area is inferred from where the marks are, not from a stated diagnosis, so Nature is 'Suspected chronic' rather than Acute.
NOTE: the exclusion list (toes, fingers, wrists) turns on near-universality, not on treatment type. Cupping is not near-universal, so it clears that bar.
26AkD5 (Scorekeeper Eye): MOSTLY FADED. Status set to Eased. (Jennie)

CUPPING BRUISES FADE ON THEIR OWN SCHEDULE, which makes them a weaker signal than tape. Tape is a daily decision and its absence means he chose not to strap it today. A fading bruise only tells you the cupping happened a while ago, not that the underlying problem improved. Read this easing as 'no fresh treatment since Day 3', not as 'the back is better'. If new marks appear, the row goes back to Active.
Booth colour the same day: 'Takerufuji has his own injury concerns', unspecified. Possibly this, possibly the right elbow and forearm on his other row.

story.html: Ura is the one who never sits still on the banzuke. He bounces from the upper maegashira down into the low teens and back up, and the crowd could not care less about his lack of silverware. What they come for is the way he wins. Ura built his reputation on acrobatic, unorthodox sumo, the kind of bout that ends with an opponent flipped over a hip or marched backward out of the ring by a plan nobody saw coming. The mawashi is cherry blossom pink, which fits him about right. He is one of the tougher outs in the division to prepare for.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Both knees in heavy bandage wrapping, not tape. First logged as its own row.

TRUE ONSET PREDATES THIS ROW. Onset Day is set to Aki 2026 Day 1 because that is the first day it was logged, not the first day it existed. Per Jennie: 'Knees are chronic for Ura, for as long as I've been watching he's been the michelin man.' Split out from the 'Ura - general / feet' row on 2026-09-24 because the visible wrapping is on the knees, not the feet, and the two are separate conditions. (Jennie)
Came in with feet problems; struggles to stay fit.

26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): BOTH KNEES in heavy bandage wrapping - 'looks like the Michelin man.' Right hand and wrist taped, left hand taped. No foot tape observed, so the visible problem is NOT where this row says it is. Knees may warrant their own row. (Jennie)
26AkD3 (Scorekeeper Eye): No tape on Ura's feet. Second look, same finding. The knees row (split out separately) is where the visible wrapping actually lives. (Jennie)

RULE SETTLED 2026-09-25 (Jennie): 'it could close a flare up but a chronic by default stays active.' Absent tape does NOT close a chronic. The activation rule closes an ACUTE item and closes a FLARE on a chronic; the chronic itself stays Active. Status stays Active and this row is no longer an open question.
STILL WORTH A LOOK, but as a different question: this row is filed as feet and the visible wrapping is on the knees. That is a row pointed at the wrong body part, not a candidate to close.

story.html: Oho carries one of the heaviest names in sumo. He is the grandson of the legendary Yokozuna Taiho, whose name meant "great roc," and Oho inherits the roc, so his own reads as "king roc." He has reached Sekiwake and Komusubi more than once. He came up as Naya. He wears a dark purple mawashi. When he is right, the joi is where he belongs.

story.html: Wakamotoharu is a former Sekiwake and the eldest of the Onami brothers, the youngest being Wakatakakage. The "waka" honors their grandfather, a former Sekiwake, and the brothers are named for the three Mori warlords. He came up as Araonami, then Goshi. He wears a black mawashi.

Bad back pain; limited pre-basho practice.
Back/buttock hampering his sumo.
Still troubled by back and buttock.

bio.v: 若元春 (Wakamotoharu) = 若 (waka, young) + 元春 (Motoharu, after the Sengoku warlord Kikkawa Motoharu) → 'Young Motoharu.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: eldest of the Onami brothers; waka- honors their grandfather ex-sekiwake Wakabayama, and the brothers' names invoke the three Mori brothers. Brother of Wakatakakage.

story.html: Wakatakakage has one of the most bittersweet lines on the board. He won the championship at the May 2026 basho from Komusubi, a career peak, and then it went sideways: a serious hip injury right before the July basho forced him out, and the crew flagged it as potentially career-altering. He is the youngest of the Onami brothers, with Wakamotoharu the eldest. His shikona reads as "young Takakage," after a Sengoku warlord. He wears a deep navy blue mawashi. The crew shorthand is WKTKKG.

layers.text: Sitting out from opening day, left thigh (official).

26NgD15 (live broadcast, Day 15.5): Booth update, named as acute compartment syndrome; hospitalized a long time, just released. Per the stable, a long road back, likely out next tournament and the provincial tours too; will fall to juryo or lower.
Still recuperating from the left-thigh injury (had surgery); sidelined from opening day, carry confirmed into Aki. [booth: Raja]
Aki2026D1: Wakatakakage is still recuperating from a left thigh injury he had surgery on. [booth, carrying]

bio.v: 若隆景 (Wakatakakage) = 若 (waka, young) + 隆景 (Takakage, after the Sengoku warlord Kobayakawa Takakage) → 'Young Takakage.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: youngest of the Onami brothers; waka- from grandfather ex-sekiwake Wakabayama; brothers named for the three Mori brothers. Brother of Wakamotoharu.

story.html: Asakoryu has spent the crew era in the lower maegashira. He is a Takasago man and the brother of Asasuiryu, the two of them sharing the "asa" family prefix. His shikona reads as "morning crimson dragon." He came up as Ishizaki. He wears a red mawashi.

layers.text: Carried in — ACL from the May contest.

bio.v: 朝紅龍 (Asakoryu) = 朝 (morning) + 紅 (crimson) + 龍 (dragon) → 'Morning crimson dragon.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: Takasago 朝- prefix; brother of Asasuiryu (both surname Ishizaki).

story.html: Tobizaru is a former Komusubi, and his name tells you how he fights: "flying monkey." The style matches it, agile and evasive, built to make bigger men miss. He is an Oitekaze man; his older brother wrestled as Hidenoumi (Kise stable) and retired in March 2026, so Tobizaru no longer has a brother competing in the top division. Both came up as Iwasaki. He wears a light grey-blue mawashi.

story.html: Asasuiryu made his top-division debut in September 2026 after a run in juryo. He is the brother of Asakoryu, and the shared "asa" prefix once caused an early scoring session to mistake the two of them for one wrestler before the crew sorted it out. A Takasago man, his shikona reads as "morning jade dragon." He came up as Ishizaki.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Band-aid on the right eye on his Makuuchi debut day. (Jennie)

bio.v: 朝翠龍 (Asasuiryu) = 朝 (morning) + 翠 (jade-green) + 龍 (dragon) → 'Morning jade dragon.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: Takasago 朝- prefix; brother of Asakoryu (both surname Ishizaki).

story.html: Wakanosho fights out of the Minatogawa stable. At the July 2026 basho he withdrew, officially with a knee, though the booth had also flagged a possible concussion from a head-first sequence the day before, and the crew deliberately kept both readings on the record rather than reconcile them. He wears a navy blue mawashi.

bio.v: 若 (waka, young) + -nosho; the remaining kanji are unverified. Confidence: LOW — flag to verify kanji. Minatogawa stable.

story.html: Shonannoumi has ranged through the lower and middle maegashira across the crew era. The name flags his home coast: Shonan, the stretch of Kanagawa coastline, plus "sea," so the shikona reads as "the Shonan sea." He is a Takadagawa man.

story.html: Hoshoryu won the Emperor's Cup at the January 2025 basho as an Ozeki, and by March 2025 he was a Yokozuna. The run has not been all smooth: he withdrew partway through the July 2026 tournament and has had stretches on the sidelines. His shikona means "ascending dragon," and the dragon is not decoration. It ties him to his uncle, the former Yokozuna Asashoryu, whose own name carried the same character. He fights in a dark navy mawashi. When he is healthy and forward, there are few better.

layers.text: Sidelined from day one, still healing from a right-knee surgery undergone after Nagoya. Distinct from the Nagoya right-thigh withdrawal (separate row). [booth: Raja]
Aki2026D1: Yokozuna Hoshoryu is sidelined from day one because he is still healing from a right knee surgery he underwent after the Nagoya Basho. [booth, carrying]

Withdrew before the day's bouts — right thigh, 'aggravated during the tournament' (JSA/booth). Kirishima receives the fusen (→11-3). 4th withdrawal since becoming yokozuna; 2nd straight basho. Scorekeeper Eye (Jennie): not buying it — reads more sore-loser than the clearly-visible injury last basho.
Carried in — returning after recuperating (out most of May).
Aggravated the R thigh — withdraws (kyujo). [origin bout vs practice unclear — verify]
26Aki Preview (0.5, air 09-11): Condition uncertain for Aki. Withdrew mid-Nagoya (kyujo); shape unknown, may not compete. [booth]
Booth attributes his Day-1 absence to a right-KNEE surgery undergone after Nagoya (logged as a separate knee row), not the thigh; thigh not mentioned today. [booth: Raja]

bio.v: 豊昇龍 (Ho-sho-ryu) = 豊 abundant + 昇 rising/ascending + 龍 dragon → 'Ascending dragon.' Confidence: HIGH (characters). Lineage echo: the 龍 dragon ties to his uncle, former yokozuna Asashoryu (朝青龍).

story.html: Kotozakura has been the picture of Ozeki consistency, holding the rank tournament after tournament without the dips that catch most men. The name is an inheritance: his grandfather was the 53rd Yokozuna, also Kotozakura, and the "koto" is the signature of the Sadogatake stable that every wrestler there carries. He came up as Kotonowaka before taking the family name. The mawashi is a light turquoise green, and the crew calls him "6 Pack."

layers.text: 5 (live, air 09-13): Booth cites chronic lower back pain this year along with knee injuries, treated with regenerative medicine. Struggling to lock opponents on the mawashi; escaped kadoban only barely in July. Watching whether he can reach double digits. [booth: Raja]
26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Left knee taped, taped below the right knee, left ankle taped. Both knees visibly involved, corroborating the booth's knee read independently. Back not observable. (Jennie)

bio.v: 琴櫃 (Koto-zakura) = 琴 koto (harp) + 櫃 zakura (cherry blossom) → 'Koto cherry blossom.' Confidence: HIGH. Inherited proper name — 琴 koto is the Sadogatake stable signature (all its wrestlers carry it); passed down from his grandfather, the 53rd yokozuna Kotozakura.

records.note: For Fujinokawa, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: Fujinokawa is one of the youngest men in the division and he has climbed like it, running up through the ranks with an Outstanding Performance prize at the July 2026 basho as a marker along the way. His shikona means "wisteria river," a name the Isenoumi stable brought back into use, and he fought earlier as Wakaikari. He wears a medium blue mawashi. The booth calls him the Mighty Mite. The crew calls him Bloody Eye.

bio.v:
Style (booth): poise and edge-defense beyond his years. Stays in contention with a resourceful last-moment grip and balance; promoted straight past Komusubi into Sekiwake. [Grand Sumo Live, booth, as of 2026-09-13]

RELENTLESS TO THE END. Murray Johnson's line for him, Aki 2026 Day 6, after Fujinokawa absorbed a leg trip, a second leg trip, an attempted sototmuso and a kubinage from Aonishiki and still won by yorikiri. Jennie: 'F just never gives up... so many techniques.' Filed here as a permanent characterisation on her call, and separately as a Catchphrase Library phrase with a Day 6 Sighting. [booth: Murray, air 2026-09-18]

Does not retreat, by his own account. Interview the same day: 'the last thing I wanted to do was retreat after we grappled with each other.' At 177cm he is the shortest man in the joi and routinely gives away 40 kilos, which is what both his nicknames are getting at from opposite directions.
藤乃川 (Fujinokawa) = 藤 (wisteria) + 乃 (poss.) + 川 (river) → 'Wisteria river.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: a revived Isenoumi-beya shikona.

story.html: Daieisho is a fixture, one of the division's dependable pusher-thrusters, a regular in the named ranks. His shikona reads as "great soaring glory." He came up under earlier names, Takanishi and then Daishoei, before settling on this one. He fights in a dark raspberry red mawashi. Japanese fans know him as the Battle Pug, and once you have seen the low, square, forward style, the name explains itself.

layers.text: Pre-tournament R leg injury limiting him.
26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Both elbows BANDAGED, both arches taped, right hand taped. No right-leg tape observed - the logged condition is not where the wrapping is. (Jennie)

26AkD2 (Scorekeeper Eye): RIGHT KNEE AND CALF TAPED. This is the right leg finally becoming visible - on Day 1 the logged condition showed nothing at all. One day apart, so either it was taped under something on Day 1 or it was aggravated in between. (Jennie)

bio.v: 大栄翔 (Daieisho) = 大 (great) + 栄 (glory/flourish) + 翔 (soar) → 'Great soaring glory.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH.

story.html: Kotoeiho rode the elevator between juryo and the bottom of makuuchi before breaking out with a Fighting Spirit prize at the July 2026 basho. He is the younger of the two Koto brothers, and the crew calls him the master of shiko: his high, balanced leg-lift stomp is a genuine crowd-pleaser and draws applause on its own. The "koto" marks him as Sadogatake, like his brother Kotoshoho, and he fought earlier as Kototebakari. The mawashi is a medium slate blue.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Right hand taped. NOTE: the left foot and ankle first noted on this bout belong to his opponent Aonishiki, not to Kotoeiho - reassigned on Jennie's confirmation. Kotoeiho has no prior injury history of any kind. (Jennie)

bio.v: Showman — signature is a beautiful, balanced high shiko (leg-lift foot stomps) that draws big applause; the crew calls him 'the master of Shiko.' Day 7: a beautifully balanced high leg stomp caught the eye again. (Jennie, 26NgD07)
琴栄峰 (Kotoeiho) = 琴 (koto, the harp) + 栄 (glory) + 峰 (peak) → 'Koto glory peak.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: Sadogatake 琴- prefix; brother of Kotoshoho (both surname Tebakari).

story.html: Yoshinofuji reached Komusubi after coming up as Kusano and then taking a shikona in the Isegahama Fuji lineage. The name reads as "Yoshino Fuji," pairing Mount Fuji with Yoshino, the region famous across Japan for its cherry blossoms. He is young, with room ahead of him.

bio.v: 吉野富士 (Yoshinofuji) = 吉野 (Yoshino, a region famed for its cherry blossoms) + 富士 (Mt. Fuji) → 'Yoshino Fuji.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Isegahama-beya (Fuji-family shikona).

story.html: Churanoumi has climbed quietly and steadily into the upper maegashira. His name is the best kind of hometown flag: he is Okinawan, and "chura umi" is the beloved Okinawan phrase for the beautiful sea, so the shikona simply means "beautiful sea." He fought earlier as Kizaki. He wears a purple mawashi.

bio.v: 美ら海 (Churanoumi) = 美ら (chura — 'beautiful' in Okinawan) + 海 (sea) → 'Beautiful sea.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: Okinawan-born; 'chura umi' is the famous Okinawan phrase for the beautiful sea.

records.note: For Fujiryoga, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: Fujiryoga is one of the division's newer faces and he came up fast. He is a Fujishima man, the "fuji" (wisteria) marking the stable, and he came up as Goshima. He is from Aichi and fights in a dark blue mawashi.

story.html: Oshoma reached Komusubi in July 2025. The Mongolian is a weight-forward, driving wrestler by design. As he told the Sumo Salon panel in Paris, he bulked up roughly 40 kilograms in six months to get there, eating three kilos of rice plus sides before bed so he was "never hungry," and settled around 160 kilograms, which he calls just right for his style. He noted his stablemaster is also foreign-born, so "he understands where I'm coming from." He fights in a light grey mawashi.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Left ankle taped, right elbow sleeve. (Jennie)

bio.v: Oshoma — the -sho-ma likely 勝馬 (victory + horse) → roughly 'victory horse,' but the first kanji is unverified. Confidence: LOW — flag to verify kanji. Naruto stable, Mongolian.

story.html: Ichiyamamoto is an upper-maegashira regular and one of the division's better characters. He worked as a civil servant before turning to sumo, and on the Sumo Salon panel he became the running "he's the exception" gag: a bread-for-breakfast holdout who loved the Paris croissants, sleeps soundly before bouts, and keeps his distance against Mongolian opponents, thrusting to stay clear of their throws. His name reads as "Yamamoto the First," his real surname with "one" set in front. He wears a jade green mawashi. The crew calls him Sleepy, and Itchy.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Left elbow sleeve, both knees taped. Predates the Day-5 lower-back row by four days; separate area. (Jennie)
First logged this basho (true onset earlier/unknown). Booth: nothing beyond what he normally carries, looked weak. [booth — verify]

Murray named a lower back problem specifically. Still no power, taken straight back and lost again to fall to 0-6; booth said he is not providing any opposition at all and hopes the injury is not threatening him. [booth, carrying]

bio.v: 一山本 (Ichiyamamoto) = 一 (one/first) + 山本 (Yamamoto, his real surname) → 'Yamamoto the First.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Context: prepends 一 (one) to his real surname.

story.html: Nishikifuji has bounced between juryo and the maegashira ranks across the crew era. He is an Isegahama man in the Fuji family of shikona, and his name reads as "brocade Fuji." He came up as Ogasawara. He wears a light plum purple mawashi.

story.html: Hiradoumi has been an upper-maegashira fixture for much of the crew era, parked around the joi tournament after tournament. The name flags his home region: Hirado, a city in Nagasaki, plus "sea," so the shikona reads as "Hirado sea." He came up as Sakaguchi. He fights in a midnight purple mawashi.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Left ankle taped. (Jennie)

bio.v: 平戸海 (Hiradoumi) = 平戸 (Hirado, a city in Nagasaki) + 海 (sea) → 'Hirado sea.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: names his home region, Hirado.

story.html: Shishi has worked through the lower and middle maegashira across the crew era. He is the division's other Ukrainian, alongside Aonishiki, and one of its bigger men at 192 centimeters. The booth has taken to comparing him to Baruto, the former Estonian Ozeki, for his balance, his fighting spirit, and how much he has improved. His shikona means "lion." He wears a black mawashi.

story.html: Kinbozan has ranged across the maegashira ranks. The Kazakh-born wrestler fights out of the Kise stable, and his shikona is a good one: "golden peak mountain," after Kinpozan, a real sacred peak. He wears a grey mawashi.

bio.v: 金峰山 (Kinbozan) = 金 (gold) + 峰山 (peak-mountain; Kinposan is a real sacred peak) → 'Golden Peak Mountain.' Confidence: HIGH. Context: Kazakh-born, Kise stable.

story.html: Shodai is a former Ozeki who has spent the crew era bouncing through the maegashira ranks. He is one of the few who fights under his own family name, so the "meaning" of the shikona is really just his surname. He wears a black mawashi. There is still enough of the former top-ranker in him to make trouble on his day.

layers.text: 26AkD2 (Scorekeeper Eye): BOOTH vs EYE DISAGREEMENT. The booth called out a left elbow injury during this bout, but nothing was wrapped or taped on it. Either it is being managed without support, or the booth is repeating the July storyline rather than reporting what is on the man today. (Jennie)

26AkD4 (Scorekeeper Eye): ELBOW STILL UNWRAPPED. Jennie's call: mark it EASED. Three days of the booth naming an elbow and nothing ever on it. The booth-vs-eye disagreement resolves in the eye's favour. (Jennie)

TWO NOTES FOR WHOEVER READS THIS NEXT. Jennie referred to this as 'the chronic' but the row is tagged Nature = Acute; worth confirming which she means before any automation keys off it. And the activation rule as written would send an acute with nothing showing to Dormant rather than Eased — Eased is her explicit call here and stands, but the two are close enough that the distinction is worth watching.

bio.v: 正代 (Shodai) = 正 (correct/upright) + 代 (generation) — but this is his real surname, so 'meaning' is incidental. Confidence: MEDIUM (real-name shikona). Context: fights under his own family name.

story.html: Asahakuryu rose out of juryo in late 2025 and established himself in the maegashira ranks. The Mongolian is a Takasago man, the "asa" prefix the same one that ran through Asashoryu, and his shikona reads as "morning white dragon." He wears a dark blue mawashi.

layers.text: 26AkD2 (Scorekeeper Eye): Tissue up one nostril at the tachiai - looks like he had a bloody nose earlier in the day, before this bout. No booth mention. Minor/cosmetic; expect to ease. (Jennie)
26AkD3 (Scorekeeper Eye): GONE. No evidence of a bloody nose. One and done. (Jennie)

It was briefly set to Eased, which was wrong by Jennie's own definition (Eased means a limp looks less gimpy or a man is getting back to his old self, not that a thing is gone). Dormant means not currently visible, and deliberately does not claim healed. First row in the log to use it.

bio.v: 朝白龍 (Asahakuryu) = 朝 (morning) + 白 (white) + 龍 (dragon) → 'Morning white dragon.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: 朝 (asa-) is the Takasago-beya signature prefix (cf. Asashoryu).

story.html: Abi is a big pusher-thruster. When his thrusting attack is on it is relentless and he can beat anyone; when it is off the results wander, which is roughly the shape of his banzuke line. His shikona reads loosely as "blaze." He came up as Horikiri. He wears a midnight blue mawashi.

layers.text: 26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Left foot taped, right hand taped. Notably one of the few with NO wrist tape. (Jennie)

bio.v: 阿炎 (Abi) = 阿 (mostly phonetic 'a'; also 'nook') + 炎 (flame/blaze) → loosely 'Blaze.' Confidence: MEDIUM — 炎 'flame' is clear, 阿 is largely a sound character.

story.html: Chiyoshoma is a wily veteran out of the Kokonoe stable. The color piece writes itself: at the July 2026 basho, on Day 9, he won his bout on his own birthday and recorded his 300th career victory the same afternoon. His shikona reads as "Chiyo's soaring horse," the "chiyo" marking the stable. He came up as Shoma. He wears a golden brown mawashi.

layers.text: Carried in — chronic lower back.
26AkD1 (Scorekeeper Eye): Right ankle taped. New area, unrelated to the back this row tracks. (Jennie)

bio.v: 千代翔馬 (Chiyoshoma) = 千代 (a thousand generations) + 翔 (soar) + 馬 (horse) → 'Chiyo's soaring horse.' Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Lineage: 千代 (chiyo-) is the Kokonoe-beya signature prefix.

story.html: Tokihayate is a Tokitsukaze man, the "toki" marking the stable, and his shikona reads roughly as "swift gale." He came up as Tokisakae.

bio.v: 時疾風 (Tokihayate) = 時 (toki, time) + 疾風 (hayate, gale / swift wind) → roughly 'swift gale.' Confidence: MEDIUM. Lineage: 時 (toki-) is the Tokitsukaze-beya signature prefix.

records.note: For Toshinofuji, Makuuchi and Crew match, since he reached makuuchi after our Jan 2025 epoch; the three-way split matters most for veterans who fought before it.

story.html: Toshinofuji made his makuuchi debut in September 2026. He is an Isegahama man in the stable's Fuji lineage, alongside names like Atamifuji, Midorifuji, and Nishikifuji, and his shikona reads as "Fuji of longevity."

bio.v: 寿之富士 — “Fuji of Longevity”: 寿 (toshi/kotobuki, long life & auspiciousness) · 之 (no, “of”) · 富士 (Mt. Fuji). The –富士/–fuji suffix marks the Isegahama-beya shikona lineage (Terunofuji, Atamifuji, Midorifuji, Nishikifuji…).
